content: I can see a corn leaf with numerous small yellowish-brown spots across the blade and darker brown/purplish spots concentrated along the midrib. This strongly suggests Physoderma brown spot. Let me verify with reference images.

The Physoderma brown spot reference (bottom-left panel) is an excellent match for the test image — showing the same pattern of numerous small yellowish-brown spots across the leaf blade with darker purplish-black spots concentrated along the midrib. The other diseases don't match: Common rust shows raised pustules, Southern rust shows orange pustules, Eyespot shows discrete circular spots with halos, SCLB shows rectangular lesions, and Holcus spot shows white/tan spots.

The key diagnostic features in the test image:
1. Numerous small yellowish-brown spots in broad bands across the leaf
2. Dark purplish-black oval spots along the midrib (distinctly darker than blade lesions)
3. Alternating bands of infected and non-infected tissue

All three are hallmark symptoms of Physoderma brown spot.
